counterfactual_missing_items: Striatal CT/MRI imaging findings are not cited by R3
Involuntary movement examination findings are not cited by R3
Elevated HbA1c is not cited by R3
decisive_items: Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg
Laboratory testing revealed a blood glucose level of 8.59 mmol/L (reference range, 3.9–6.1) and a hemoglobin A1c of 7.43% (4–6)
Subsequent brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia.
response.rationale: R2 uniquely integrates the untreated diabetic context and hyperglycemia with the characteristic bilateral striatal CT hyperdensity and T1 hyperintensity on MRI, matching diabetic striatopathy. R3 captures the diabetic cause but omits the imaging and movement evidence; R1 describes the movement syndrome and imaging but misses the diabetic cause.

rejected.why: Hemichorea-hemiballismus is a phenotypic label supported by movement and imaging spans, but it omits the diabetic history and hyperglycemia that identify the underlying cause, making it less complete than R2.
